Question_text: Autobrake is a business that manufactures brake systems for cars. Fig. 1 shows its market share in 2005 and 2010. The market for brake systems was worth $70m in 2010. It is likely to become an increasingly competitive market. Autobrake's management believe that the company needs to develop a wider range of products if it is to be profitable in the future.
image: A horizontal bar chart titled 'Market shares for brake systems'. It compares the market share for 'Autobrake' and 'other companies' for two years: 2005 and 2010. The y-axis represents the 'year' (2005 and 2010), and the x-axis represents '% market share' from 0 to 100 in increments of 20. A legend indicates that a striped bar represents 'Autobrake' and a plain bar represents 'other companies'. In 2005, Autobrake has approximately 20% market share, and other companies have 80%. In 2010, Autobrake has approximately 40% market share, and other companies have 60%.
Unit: UNIT 1: Understanding business activity, UNIT 3: Marketing, UNIT 4: Operations management
Topic: 1.5 Business objectives and stakeholder objectives, 3.1 Marketing, competition and the customer, 3.3 Marketing mix, 4.1 Production of goods and services
Sub_topic: Different objectives: survival, growth, profit, market share
Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production

Parts.part_text: What is meant by an ‘increasingly competitive market'?
Calculate the value of Autobrake's sales in 2010.
Autobrake uses flow production in its factories. Identify and explain two benefits of using flow production.
Identify and explain three possible reasons why Autobrake's market share changed between 2005 and 2010.
Do you think that investing in a wider range of products will mean that the business will become more profitable in the future? Justify your answer.

Question_text: The economy of country A is in recession. To deal with the problems caused by the recession, the Government has cut interest rates and reduced taxes. These changes have had a big impact on businesses in country A. The Government has also introduced laws to protect employees at work. Some people have suggested that the Government should give grants and subsidies to private sector businesses to help them survive.
Unit: UNIT 6: External influences on business activity, UNIT 2: People in business, UNIT 1: Understanding business activity
Topic: 6.1 Economic issues, 2.3 Recruitment, selection and training of employees, 1.3 Enterprise, business growth and size
Sub_topic: Stages of business cycle: growth, boom, recession, slump
Legal controls: contracts, unfair dismissal, discrimination, health/safety, minimum wage
Government support for start-ups, grants, training schemes

Parts.part_text: What is meant by the term 'recession'?
Identify two ways in which consumers might be affected by a recession.
Identify and explain two consequences of a fall in interest rates on businesses in country A.
Identify and explain three ways by which employees can be protected at work by Government laws.
Do you think that Governments should give financial support to private sector businesses to survive in a recession? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Sarah set up a business as a sole trader running a nursery for small children too young to go to school. The business is successful and has opened a number of new nurseries. Sarah took on a business partner in 2007. Growth has continued and now the business has 10 nurseries in different towns and villages. Sarah is planning to open another nursery and is looking for a suitable location.
Unit: UNIT 1: Understanding business activity, UNIT 4: Operations management
Topic: 1.4 Types of business organisation, 1.2 Classification of businesses, 1.3 Enterprise, business growth and size, 4.4 Location decisions
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures

Parts.part_text: What is meant by the term 'sole trader'?
A nursery school is classified as a tertiary sector activity. Identify two other examples of businesses that are also in the tertiary sector.
Identify and explain two advantages to Sarah of having a business partner.
Identify and explain three factors Sarah should consider when choosing a suitable location for a new nursery.
Do you think that it would be a good idea for Sarah to continue to expand her business? Justify your answer.
